findings.description: The adapter's label-write success check is unsound because `/issues/update` never returns a non-2xx status on failure. `agent-coordinator/src/coordination_api.py:1389-1419` returns `{"success": false, "reason": ...}` with HTTP 200 for every failure path it has: `ValueError` from `UUID(request.issue_id)` or from `service.update` (line 1411-1412), any other exception (line 1413-1415), and `issue is None` / `issue_not_found` (line 1417-1418). The bridge's `_normalize_operation_response` (`skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/coordination_bridge.py:489-508`) maps any 2xx to `{"status": "ok"}` without reading `response.success`. So `queue_projection.py:102` (`if labelled.get("status") != "ok"`) and `:136` (`if cleared.get("status") != "ok"`) both pass on a failed write, and the adapter returns `{"status": "ok", ...}` at line 139. `persist_and_project` (`skills/autopilot/scripts/autopilot.py:206-218`) then classifies the transition as a healthy projection and logs nothing. This directly violates the spec scenario 'Projection outage is degraded, not authoritative': 'a failed canonical-row label update or stale-label cleanup SHALL also report projection degradation with a bounded reason'. A compounding path makes it reachable without any DB fault: migration 035 (`agent-coordinator/database/migrations/035_work_queue_projection.sql:128-137`) can return `success=TRUE` with `v_id` NULL, and `_projection_mutation_payload` (`coordination_api.py:132`) stringifies that to the literal `"None"`, which passes the adapter's `isinstance(task_id, str) and task_id` guard at line 91-93 and is then sent as `issue_id` to `/issues/update`.
findings.resolution: In `try_projection_issue_update` (and `try_projection_issue_list`), treat a 2xx envelope whose `response.success` is not `True` as a failure — e.g. return `{"status": "failed", "reason": response.get("reason", "issue_update_rejected")}` — or have the adapter check `_response(labelled).get("success") is True` in addition to the transport status. Separately, make `_projection_mutation_payload` reject a NULL `task_id` rather than emitting `"None"`.
findings.failure_scenario: Coordinated Autopilot advances PLAN -> PLAN_REVIEW. `try_submit_work` succeeds and returns the canonical `task_id`. The follow-up `/issues/update` fails (row concurrently deleted, malformed id, or a transient service exception caught at coordination_api.py:1413) and answers HTTP 200 `{"success": false, "reason": "issue_not_found"}`. The adapter returns `{"status": "ok"}`; `persist_and_project` reports success and emits no warning. The canonical row never receives `change:<id>` / `projection:autopilot-phase`, so migration 037's `notify_work_queue_change` label branch never fires, no `projection.labels_changed` event is published, no SSE snapshot is refreshed, and `_build_snapshot`'s `list_issues(labels=["change:<cid>"])` (`event_stream.py:181`) cannot see the row. The kanban board silently shows the previous phase forever while the operator is told the projection is healthy.

findings.description: Every bridge helper the adapter calls re-runs full coordinator capability detection. `_execute_single_endpoint_operation` (`skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/coordination_bridge.py:530`) unconditionally calls `detect_coordination`, which issues one `GET /health` (line 397), one probe per entry in `_CAPABILITY_PROBES` — eight of them (line 55-68) — and one `GET /search/code/status` (line 428): ten HTTP round-trips before the one request that does the work. There is no memoization anywhere in the module. The adapter is the first caller to chain helpers at scale: a reconcile pass issues 1 reconcile + 1 canonical label write + 1 list + up to `_MAX_CLEANUP_ROWS = 100` sequential label clears (line 129-137) = up to 103 helper calls, i.e. roughly 1,133 serialized HTTP requests, each with `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1.5` (`coordination_bridge.py:22`). This runs on `run_loop`'s synchronous critical path via `persist_and_project` (`skills/autopilot/scripts/autopilot.py:1008`, `:1147`) and blocks the phase loop. Even on a fast local coordinator at ~20 ms/request that is ~23 s for one reconcile; the spec scenario 'Live phase transition is mirrored' requires the phase to be exposed 'within 5 seconds'. The ordinary submit path is not free either: 2-3 helpers = 22-33 requests per phase edge, and the same cost is paid again by every `runner.py project-state` invocation the SKILL.md protocol mandates after each runner mutation.
findings.resolution: Cache the `detect_coordination` result for the lifetime of one adapter call (pass the resolved state into the helpers, or add a short-lived memo keyed by `(http_url, api_key)`), and/or add a batch label-clear endpoint so the cleanup loop is one request instead of up to 100. Also consider probing only the `capability_flag` the operation actually needs rather than all nine.
findings.failure_scenario: Coordinated Autopilot resumes a change whose previous run left 60 stale double-labelled projection rows. `run_loop` calls `persist_and_project(..., mode="reconcile")` at autopilot.py:1008 before any phase work. The adapter makes 63 helper calls; each one re-runs the 10-request detection sweep, so ~693 serialized HTTP requests fire before the loop can start its first phase. With a coordinator answering in ~50 ms the resume stalls ~35 s; if any single capability endpoint hangs, each of the 63 sweeps burns the full 1.5 s timeout on that probe, adding ~95 s. The 5-second exposure requirement in the spec is missed and the operator sees the loop apparently hung at startup.

findings.description: Migration 037 adds the `AND task_type <> 'issue'` claim exclusion to only one of three coexisting `claim_task` overloads. A database that has applied 001 through 037 holds `claim_task(TEXT, TEXT, TEXT[])` from `001_core_schema.sql:212-217`, `claim_task(TEXT, TEXT, TEXT[], TEXT[], INTEGER)` from `021_agent_requirements.sql:19-24`, and the six-argument form from `027_claim_task_exclude_submitter.sql:10-16` which 037 replaces. Neither older overload is dropped, and both still contain the unfiltered `WHERE status = 'pending' AND (p_task_types IS NULL OR ...)` predicate — so any caller reaching them claims projection rows. The spec requirement is absolute: 'Every `task_type=issue` row SHALL be excluded from all work claims.' Migration 035 established the exact remedy for this class of problem in this codebase: `035_work_queue_projection.sql:11` does `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS coordinator_notify(TEXT,TEXT,TEXT,TEXT,TEXT)` with the comment 'Calls with five arguments are otherwise ambiguous once both migrations have been applied', and line 66 does the same for the stale `submit_task` signature. 037 skips that step. The production service path is currently safe only incidentally, because `work_queue.py:399-408` always passes all six named parameters; the invariant is not enforced by the schema.
findings.resolution: Add `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS claim_task(TEXT,TEXT,TEXT[]);` and `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS claim_task(TEXT,TEXT,TEXT[],TEXT[],INTEGER);` before the `CREATE OR REPLACE` in 037, mirroring the pattern already used at 035_work_queue_projection.sql:11 and :66, so exactly one claim entry point exists and the exclusion cannot be bypassed.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator or maintenance script runs `SELECT claim_task('agent-1', 'claude_code')` against a migrated database — a three-argument call that binds the surviving 001 overload. That overload has no `task_type <> 'issue'` predicate, so it selects and claims the priority-1 `task_type=issue` Autopilot projection row (projection rows use priority 1, so they sort first under `ORDER BY priority ASC, created_at ASC`). The row flips to `status='claimed'` with `attempt_count` incremented, migration 037's status branch fires a spurious `task.claimed` SSE transition for the change, and the board reports the current phase as claimed work assigned to an agent that will never complete it.

findings.description: There is no recovery path from a `stale_projection` conflict, and nothing ever resets the projection head. `work_queue_projection_heads` is created in `035_work_queue_projection.sql:52-57` and rows are only ever inserted or upserted (`:108`, `:167-170`); a repository-wide search finds no DELETE or reset of that table in any production code path — the only other references are test fixtures (`agent-coordinator/tests/integration/postgres/conftest.py:30`). Meanwhile `loop-state.json` is per-change-directory and disappears when the change is archived or an operator restarts a run. `_requires_reconciliation` (line 142-151) advances through reconciliation only for `reconciliation_required`, which is correct per the spec ('only a bridge `status=error`, HTTP-409 problem response whose `response.detail` is `reconciliation_required` SHALL advance through reconciliation rather than degrade'), so a `stale_projection` reply from `035_work_queue_projection.sql:110-112` falls to `_degraded` at line 89-90 and is only logged as a warning by `persist_and_project` (`autopilot.py:206-217`). The result is a durably wedged projection with no documented remedy: the change's board entry is pinned to the previous run's generation until the new run's `total_iterations` happens to exceed the old head, and `docs/guides/work-queue-truth-projection.md` claims 'Projection outages are a degradation... The next coordinated resume reconciles from `loop-state.json`', which is not true for this case.
findings.resolution: Give the head table a lifecycle: either clear the `work_queue_projection_heads` row (and the change's projection rows) when a change is archived by `cleanup-feature`, or add an explicit operator-facing reset — e.g. a `runner.py project-state --mode reset` that calls a coordinator endpoint to drop the head. At minimum, surface `stale_projection` distinctly in the degraded reason and document the manual remedy in `docs/guides/work-queue-truth-projection.md` under 'Failure recovery'.
findings.failure_scenario: Change `my-feature` runs to DONE at `total_iterations = 14`, leaving `work_queue_projection_heads` at sequence 14. `cleanup-feature` archives the OpenSpec directory, so `openspec/changes/my-feature/loop-state.json` is gone. The change is later reopened and Autopilot is re-run: `runner.py init` creates a fresh state at `(INIT, 0)`, and `run_loop` line 1023 projects it. `submit_task` takes the `v_seq < v_head_seq` branch and returns `stale_projection`; the adapter degrades. Every subsequent transition (seq 1, 2, 3 ...) degrades the same way for the next fourteen phase edges. Throughout, the board keeps displaying the stale DONE-generation row as the current phase, and the only signal is a `logger.warning` in the loop's output.

findings.description: The three new subcommands break the exit-code contract the rest of `runner.py` establishes and that SKILL.md now keys the projection protocol off. The existing convention is exit 2 for caller/validation errors and exit 1 for operational failures: `_cmd_apply_outcome` returns 2 for `ValueError` and 1 for other exceptions (line 358-363), `_cmd_record_state_only_archetype` does the same (line 322-325), as does `_cmd_build_dispatch` (line 295-298); `_cmd_init` correctly follows it (2 at line 374, 1 at line 388). `_cmd_transition` (line 401-403) collapses `ValueError` — raised both by `phase_agent._validate_change_id` for a bad `--change-id` and by `transition()` for an unknown `--outcome` — into exit 1, and `_cmd_project_state` (line 420-422) inverts the convention by returning 2 for `OSError`, which here is the operational case of a missing `loop-state.json`, while returning 1 for a genuinely degraded projection at line 427. Worse, `_cmd_transition` lists `autopilot.GatePending` in the same `except` clause as real errors. `_cmd_apply_outcome:338-349` handles the identical parked-gate condition deliberately and comments why: 'Exit 0 — this is a stop, not a failure (the caller's escalation wrapper treats non-zero as a fault to escalate).' `_cmd_transition` returns 1 for that same state, and the newly added SKILL.md line 'A failed transition is a stop: do not project and do not advance work' gives the host no way to tell a parked gate from a broken run.
findings.resolution: Split `_cmd_transition`'s handler: `except autopilot.GatePending` -> write the explanatory stderr message and `return 0` (matching `_cmd_apply_outcome:338-349`), `except ValueError` -> `return 2`, `except OSError` -> `return 1`. In `_cmd_project_state`, separate `except ValueError -> 2` from `except OSError -> 1` so a missing state file is reported as an operational failure rather than a caller error. Then state the code table explicitly in the SKILL.md projection protocol next to the existing gate-check 0/3/4 table.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate is parked for change `demo` (`state.pending_gate` is set and persisted). The host, following SKILL.md's 'Canonical phase edges' section, runs `runner.py transition --change-id demo --outcome proceed`. `_apply_transition` raises `GatePending` at autopilot.py:799-800 before mutating anything; `_cmd_transition` catches it, prints 'runner: transition failed: ...' and exits 1. Per the protocol's 'A failed transition is a stop' rule combined with the escalation-wrapper behavior documented at runner.py:342-343, the host treats the normal awaiting-a-human state as a run fault and escalates — where the same condition reached through `apply-outcome` would have exited 0 with a message telling the operator to run `gate-answer`.

findings.description: Three parity gaps remain between the updated contract and the runtime. (a) Lines 102 and 135 declare `"401": {description: Missing or invalid X-API-Key}` with no content, but `projection_http_problem_handler` (`agent-coordinator/src/coordination_api.py:854-870`) matches on `request.url.path in {"/work/submit", "/work/reconcile"}` and `exc.status_code in {401, 403}` — so 401 on exactly these two paths returns `application/problem+json` with the same four-field body the contract already models as `Problem`; only the 403 half of that handler is documented. (b) The `"200"` entries at lines 101 and 134 carry no schema, so `cancelled_task_ids` is undocumented even though it is the field `skills/autopilot/scripts/queue_projection.py:107` reads to drive stale-label cleanup, and `coordination_api.py:1215-1216` has non-obvious behavior around it (the key is popped when no `projection_key` was supplied). (c) The `/work/submit` request body (lines 88-99) omits `agent_requirements`, which `WorkSubmitRequest` accepts (`coordination_api.py:225`). The `Problem` schema itself, the `ProjectionKey` shape, and the 403/409/422 problem+json responses all match the runtime exactly — this is the residue, not a systemic mismatch.
findings.resolution: Point the two `"401"` entries at `#/components/responses/Problem403`-equivalent problem+json content (or add a `Problem401` response reusing the `Problem` schema), add a response schema for the `"200"` cases that includes `task_id`, `created`, `deduplicated`, `status`, and `cancelled_task_ids`, and add `agent_requirements` to the `/work/submit` request body properties.
findings.failure_scenario: A client generated from this contract calls `/work/submit` without a valid `X-API-Key`, expects an opaque or `application/json` 401 body per the spec, and receives `application/problem+json`. A strict generated client with content-type-driven deserialization fails to parse the response and surfaces a transport error rather than the authentication failure. Separately, an independent consumer implementing stale-row cleanup from the contract alone has no way to know `cancelled_task_ids` exists on the 200 response, so it cannot reproduce the cleanup behavior the adapter depends on.

findings.description: Positive observation — the SSE coalescing, backpressure, and unsubscribe axis is sound, including the round-1 fix. `_on_task_event` (line 276-280) latches `projection_refresh_pending` before enqueuing a single marker, so the 101-row label burst produced by one reconcile pass collapses to one marker. Both consumption paths reset the latch at the correct point: line 324 clears it before the `await _build_snapshot` on line 327, and line 346 clears it after the synchronous `get_nowait` drain at 338-342 but before the `await` at 347. In both cases an event arriving during snapshot construction re-latches and enqueues exactly one follow-up, so a refresh can neither be lost nor duplicated unboundedly — that is precisely the backpressure-drain hole the round-1 review flagged, and it is closed. The `finally` block at 355-360 removes both bus callbacks by closure identity on every exit path (normal close, `CancelledError`, unexpected exception), preserving the leak fix documented at line 291-301. `_make_transition` still normalizes `from`/`to` against the state enum, and the projection marker returns early rather than being routed through it, so no malformed transition is emitted for a label-only change. The only cost is cosmetic: a marker consumed at line 320-328 immediately before the window trips at 336 pays for a snapshot that is then discarded and rebuilt.

Positive observation — the trigger's change-id routing is correct on both label directions, which is what makes label removal observable. The label branch (line 71-76) fires only when `OLD.labels IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.labels` and the projection label is present in either array, so ordinary issue edits do not generate projection events. It then prefers a `change:` label from `NEW.labels` and falls back to `OLD.labels` (line 78-89) — the case that matters, because the adapter clears stale rows with `labels=[]` (`queue_projection.py:132`), leaving `NEW.labels` empty; without the OLD fallback the removal event would carry `change_id = NULL` and be dropped by the SSE filter at `event_stream.py:274`. `substr(v_label, 8)` correctly strips the seven-character `change:` prefix, matching migration 025's convention. The status branch correctly resets `v_change_id := NULL` at line 96 before its own scan, so a label-derived id from the first branch cannot leak into a status event. `COALESCE(..., ARRAY[]::TEXT[])` guards every `FOREACH` against NULL label arrays, and `task_type` is `NOT NULL` (`001_core_schema.sql:32`) so the new `task_type <> 'issue'` predicate has no three-valued-logic hazard.

Positive observation — `enter_escalate` sequencing is now correct and idempotent. The guard `if state.current_phase != "ESCALATE"` (line 505) makes the phase change, the `previous_phase` capture, and the `total_iterations += 1` a single atomic group, so a direct escalation produces a genuinely new projection identity `(change_id, "ESCALATE", n+1)` exactly once. That closes the concrete failure it was written for: previously the phase moved to ESCALATE while `total_iterations` stayed put, so `submit_task` saw `v_seq = v_head_seq AND v_phase <> v_head_phase` and returned `projection_generation_mismatch` (`035_work_queue_projection.sql:113-115`) — a conflict the adapter deliberately does not reconcile through, which would have stranded every escalation as a permanently degraded projection. Re-entering `enter_escalate` while already in ESCALATE now updates only `escalation_reason` and `phase_started_at`, so the key is stable and the second call deduplicates against the existing row instead of drifting the sequence. Both call sites in `run_loop` (line 1075 for a phase exception, line 1120 for `GoalGateRefused`) route through it and then persist-and-project, so no path enters ESCALATE durably while the previous queue generation stays live.

Positive observation — coordinator-free isolation is enforced structurally, not just by convention. `queue_projection` is imported lazily inside `_cmd_project_state` (line 413) rather than at module scope, and `queue_projection.py` itself is the only module that performs the `sys.path` insertion for the bridge (line 11-16), so a local-parallel or sequential host never loads the publisher or its transport dependency. On the in-process side `run_loop`'s `queue_projection_fn` defaults to `None` and `persist_and_project` short-circuits to `{"status": "skipped", "reason": "projection_callback_absent"}` (`autopilot.py:199-200`) before touching any network code, so the callback-free tier's behavior is byte-identical to the pre-change loop. The guarantee is pinned from two independent directions: `test_phase_projection_isolation.py:12-27` AST-parses both `autopilot.py` and `runner.py` and asserts no top-level `queue_projection` import, and `:47-86` monkeypatches all four projection transport helpers to `pytest.fail` and then drives a full `run_loop` with `queue_projection_fn=None`. The direction-of-truth invariant also holds: the adapter reads only `change_id`, `current_phase`, and `total_iterations` off `LoopState` and returns a plain envelope, and `persist_and_project` never writes any part of that envelope back into the state, so no queue response can become a state-machine input.

Positive observation — the exact nested 409 reconciliation matches the runtime byte for byte, and the round-1 problem-shape fix holds. `_requires_reconciliation` (line 142-151) requires all four of `status == "error"`, `status_code == 409`, a dict `response`, and `response["detail"] == "reconciliation_required"`. That is exactly what the runtime produces: `projection_problem_handler` (`coordination_api.py:833-852`) emits `{"type", "title", "status", "detail"}` with `detail` set to the raw reason string, `_projection_mutation_payload:123-124` maps `reconciliation_required` to status 409 via `_PROJECTION_CONFLICTS`, and the bridge's `_normalize_operation_response:509-517` places the parsed body under `response` with `status` `"error"` for a non-2xx. `_http_request` parses the body regardless of the `application/problem+json` content type (line 322-328), so the nested `detail` is reachable. The narrowness is deliberate and spec-mandated, and `test_queue_projection.py:100-115` pins the negative by asserting a 409 carrying `projection_generation_mismatch` degrades without calling reconcile. Sibling conflicts are correctly routed elsewhere: 403 and 401 become `_skipped_operation` (`coordination_bridge.py:483-488`) and 422 stays an error — all non-`ok`, all funnelled into `_degraded`. Exclusive ownership on the list path is also sound, since `IssueService.list_issues` documents and implements AND semantics on `labels` (`issue_service.py:302`, `:340-344`) and pre-filters on `task_type=eq.issue` (`:314`), so the reconcile-mode cleanup can only ever see this change's own double-labelled projection rows.
